title: Typed values in Java
summary: Declare typed values, branch on a condition, and count with a for-each loop.

scenario.briefing: The campus inventory report needs a reliable count of positive stock changes. Implement the count in Java and keep the types explicit.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

Use if (value > 0) { count += 1; } inside the loop.

misconceptions.feedback: Use .equals for text. == asks whether two references point to the same object.

sections.title: Java values and decisions
sections.body: Java declares every variable with a type: int count = 3; double price = 12.50; boolean ready = true; and String name = "Ada". Primitive types hold numbers and booleans directly. String is a reference type, and == compares references while .equals compares text. An if statement selects a branch, and switch can select among several constant cases. A for-each loop visits every array element: for (int value : values) { ... }.
